name: Fried's Tooth and Nail Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Fried's Tooth and Nail Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of congenital nail dystrophy affecting fingernails and toenails
Hypodontia or oligodontia with abnormal tooth morphology
Sparse or brittle hair with structural abnormalities
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital nail dystrophy and hypodontia with abnormal tooth morphology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by family history and exclusion of other ectodermal dysplasias

pathognomonic.notes: Involves both fingernails and toenails with nail hypoplasia or dysplasia
Missing teeth and malformed teeth including conical or peg-shaped teeth
Hair may be sparse, fragile, or have abnormal shaft morphology

common.notes: Permanent teeth eruption delayed compared to normal age
Separation of the nail plate from the nail bed
Hair shafts appear thin and fragile under microscopy
Thickening of skin on palms and soles
searchTerms: thickened skin on palms and soles
mild palm and foot skin thickening
slight keratin buildup on hands and feet

occasional.notes: Defective enamel formation leading to thin or pitted enamel

rare.notes: Subtle facial features such as midface hypoplasia
Wing-like extension of skin over nail plate

laboratory: Hair shaft microscopy showing structural abnormalities
imaging: Dental X-rays revealing hypodontia and abnormal tooth morphology
genetic: Mutations in genes related to ectodermal development (e.g., MSX1, PAX9) reported in some cases
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Broader ectodermal involvement including sweat gland abnormalities
More severe hair and skin involvement
Presence of patellar hypoplasia or aplasia
Renal involvement and iliac horns on imaging

redFlags: Severe nail dystrophy with secondary infection
Marked hypodontia causing feeding or speech difficulties
Family history of similar symptoms suggesting genetic counseling need
references: Orphanet: Fried's Tooth and Nail Syndrome - ORPHA:99672
Clinical Dermatology Textbooks describing nail and tooth dysplasias
